note: Set A keeps the D5 laundry millwork callouts correctly separated: 3/4" MDF GABLE FIN. W/ P3 as the gable finish and STEEL L-BRACKET ATTACHMENT as a separate attachment item, whereas Set B fuses them into a single invented 'P3 STEEL L-BRACKET' attachment and drops the gable finish. Set A also correctly treats WHITE THINSET MORTAR as the tile adhesive and keeps the 3/8" porcelain wall tile distinct from the glass backsplash tile; Set B labels the thinset as the 'backsplash material' and reuses the vague name 'bathroom wall tile' for both the porcelain tile and the glass tile. Both sets share the same invented '3/4" MDF EDGE STRIP' quote (the text layer lists EDGE STRIP separately from the 3/4" MDF gable) and the spurious 'direction E' condition, and both duplicate the D1 scale and glass-tile dimension claims.
remarks: Both sets fabricate the quote '3/4" MDF EDGE STRIP'; in the text layer 'EDGE STRIP' and '3/4" MDF GABLE FIN. W/ P3' are separate D5 callouts, so the 3/4" MDF dimension belongs to the gable. Both also add 'direction E' to the 1/4" per foot slope; the 'E' in the text layer is a drawing grid/bubble label, not a slope direction. Both omit BLOCKING AS REQ'D, WATERPROOF MEMBRANE, THIN SET, LINE OF FIN. COUNTERTOP, and the D5 scale (1 1/2" = 1'-0"). PT1 is tagged to the finished bathroom floor/subfloor area in the text layer, so binding it to 'shower pan' (both sets) or to a generic 'surface' (Set B) is questionable.
